channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Zoning – Standing
item.description: Where a complaint challenging the creation of a new zoning district in a Massachusetts town was dismissed for lack of standing, the dismissal order should be upheld because the plaintiffs have not adequately demonstrated that they have been or likely will be injured in fact.

item.title: Immigration – Moral turpitude – Open and gross lewdness
item.description: Where a lawful permanent resident was ordered removed after he was twice convicted under Massachusetts law (G.L.c. 272, §16) for “open and gross lewdness,” a decision by the Board of Immigration Appeals affirming the removal order should be reversed because §16 is not categorically a “crime involving moral turpitude” (CIMT) under the Immigration and Nationality Act.

item.title: Probation Service speeds up process for sealing criminal records
item.description: The Massachusetts Probation Service cut criminal record sealing wait times to under 30 days, easing barriers to jobs, housing, and second chances.

item.title: PI defendant not insured by grandmother’s homeowner’s policy
item.description: The Appeals Court ruled a homeowner’s policy did not cover a $300,000 injury judgment against an adult grandson despite claims of financial dependence.

item.title: Federal judge allows Vineyard Wind project to resume
item.description: A federal judge allowed Vineyard Wind to resume construction after the Trump administration halted offshore wind projects over national security concerns.

item.title: Trump administration sued over 2 deaths in boat strike off Venezuela’s coast
item.description: Families of two men killed in a US missile strike filed a wrongful death lawsuit, alleging unlawful killings under maritime and international law.

item.title: Second medical malpractice suit filed in Lindsay Clancy case
item.description: Lindsay Clancy filed a medical malpractice lawsuit alleging negligent mental health treatment worsened her postpartum condition before her children’s deaths.

item.title: TikTok settles youth social media addiction lawsuit
item.description: TikTok agreed to settle a landmark lawsuit alleging its platform fueled youth addiction and mental health harm, as trials proceed against Meta and YouTube.

item.title: Appeals Court judge denies Gabriel House’s bid to access insurance money
item.description: A single judge of the Appeals Court has denied an attempt by the owners of Gabriel House to access their insurance money, without which the owners said the fire-damaged building could fall apart.

item.title: Consumer class action accuses Red Sox of ‘drip pricing’
item.description: A consumer class action alleges the Boston Red Sox used drip pricing and junk fees to hide ticket costs, violating Massachusetts and Rhode Island consumer laws.
